key_insight: Beacon reframes agentic visual reasoning around two core abilities: knowing when to use tools and knowing how to use them effectively. The goal is not more reasoning steps, but better task success through smarter tool invocation.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the inefficiency and unreliability of agentic visual reasoning in multimodal large language models, where models may overuse tools, use them at the wrong time, or apply them poorly.
method: Introduces two dimensions for evaluating tool use in MLLMs: Mode Adaptiveness (when to use tools) and Tool Effect (how well tools improve outcomes).
Reinterprets agentic visual reasoning as a decision problem focused on task success rather than elaborate reasoning chains.
Provides a framework for assessing whether tool use is necessary, appropriately timed, and beneficial for visual reasoning tasks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Beacon offers a clearer way to design and evaluate tool-using MLLMs that are more efficient and effective on complex multimodal tasks. It can help reduce unnecessary tool calls while improving overall performance and usability.

paper_title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning
paper_authors: Qixun Wang, Yang Shi, Letian Cheng, Zhuoran Zhang, Yan He
